impl.summary: The evaluation harness has a splat suite (scripts/eval/cases/splat.json, kind video) that compares Idol 3D Best and Quick against TripoSplat as it ships, plus Idol with the photo crop on the 3 photo cases. It scores the orbit video with DINOv2 style against the input picture, temporal and aesthetic, and adds an optional cheap 'splat' metric that reads the .spz or .ply for the share of Gaussians under opacity 0.05 (haze). A fal TripoSplat reference variant, labelled TripoSplat and cloud-only, is included. The harness gained variant 'tags' (run only on tagged cases) and the suite default 'styleModel' (kept in run.json and used when --style-model isn't given). docs/research/idol-9.md has a 'Results (pending a GPU run)' section with the commands, what each number decides and an empty results table. §3 and §7.2 are untouched, and no default (MODELS_3D.splat.open, IDOL_PRESETS) was changed.
built: scripts/eval/cases/splat.json: 11 cases (bottle, sneaker, headphones renders; mug, handbag, figurine photos tagged photo; stylised character; person; chair; plant; glass-chrome), 3 seeds, inputs local/splat/*, demoInputs from fixtures/, references = the input picture. Variants: idol-best (candidate; 50 euler cfg 4 262144), idol-quick (20 dpmpp_2m cfg 4 65536), triposplat-today (graph defaults), idol-photo-crop (best + photoCrop true + cropMode real, tags photo), triposplat-cloud (fal triposplat, cloud only). defaults.styleModel dinov2; 'decides' field holds the three rules.

scripts/eval/lib/schema.mjs: METRICS gains 'splat'; Variant.tags (refused when no case carries the tag); defaults.styleModel (clip|dinov2). case.schema.json regenerated by gen-cases.mjs (no other generated file changed).

scripts/eval/lib/plan.mjs: a variant with tags skips cases without them, and says so in the skip reason. run.mjs writes styleModel into run.json; eval.mjs scoring uses --style-model, else run.json's styleModel.

scripts/eval/metrics/fuobe_metrics/splat.py (numpy only): opacities from .spz v1-3 and binary 3DGS .ply, detected by content; haze share and count. score.py: m_splat family, 3D files counted in the fingerprint, and a 'preview' still beside a clip is no longer scored (Idol's clean graph renders the input view, which would inflate style). registry.py and metric-info.mjs: haze (lower is better, tie 0.01) and gaussians.
scripts/eval/README.md: suites table row, local/splat inputs, variant tags and defaults.styleModel, the splat metric row, and a 'The splat suite' section with the commands.
docs/research/idol-9.md: 'Results (pending a GPU run)' section before §10.

findings.summary: Rule (1) in `decides` (repeated in docs/research/idol-9.md Results, item 1) asks for 'at least 6 [blind ratings] per case' for idol-best against triposplat-today. With 3 seeds, the review page offers only 3 such pairs per case.
findings.failure_scenario: buildPairs (scripts/eval/lib/review.mjs L62-75) pairs the candidate with each alternative once per key (case and seed). With seeds [1001, 2002, 3003], one reviewer gets 3 idol-best vs triposplat-today pairs per case, so the rule's '6 per case' can't be met unless a second person rates or the 6 counts every alternative (the promote rule's reading: Quick and the photo crop as well). The rule as written is ambiguous or can't be met for one reviewer. Suggested fix: say '6 per case across the alternatives (every pair offered)', or ask for two reviewers.

findings.summary: The command list includes `pnpm eval:promote latest`. That judges idol-best against every alternative (idol-quick and idol-photo-crop too), so its per-case verdict is not decision (1) in `decides`.
findings.failure_scenario: promote() (scripts/eval/lib/compare.mjs L187) uses every other variant when --against isn't given. A case where idol-photo-crop beats idol-best on style is put 'on hold' even if Idol beats TripoSplat there, and someone reading that output as the Splat-default verdict would decide wrongly. `pnpm eval:promote latest --against triposplat-today` is the command that matches rule (1). Docs only; no code is affected.

findings.summary: The triposplat-cloud variant hasn't been run (no fal key here), and fal's ~$0.05 per job is the catalog's figure, not re-checked at the source. At 33 jobs that is about $1.65, under DEFAULT_CLOUD_CAP of $5.
findings.failure_scenario: None seen. The request has no `op`, but inferOperation (src/lib/catalog/plan.ts L37-76) falls through to routes[0].op = 'splat'. The fal .ply comes back as kind model3d, and splat.py reads it by its content.

fix.finalSummary: idol-3 adds a 'splat' evaluation suite: Idol 3D Best and Quick against TripoSplat as it ships, plus Idol with the photo crop on the 3 photo cases. It scores the orbit video on DINOv2 style against the input picture, temporal and aesthetic, and adds a numpy 'splat' haze metric read from the .spz or .ply. There is also a cloud-only fal TripoSplat reference variant labelled TripoSplat. This fix makes the decision rules ask for blind ratings one reviewer can actually give, and names the promote command that checks decision 1 (--against triposplat-today). Open engine: built and checked by schema validation, a demo dry run, a demo run and pytest. Real numbers need an 8-16 GB GPU with both models' weights and the metrics venv with torch and DINOv2. Cloud engine: only the triposplat-cloud reference variant (fal's hosted TripoSplat; no Idol on the cloud because it isn't hosted). It is priced under the harness spend cap and has not run because there's no fal key here. Demo: the suite runs end to end, but demo numbers decide nothing. Public sign-up: unaffected. This is a developer harness under scripts/eval plus docs, with no route, page or run path, so guests and accounts see nothing new. Accounts still can't start any 3D model (own-gpu-tool). No defaults changed (MODELS_3D.splat.open, IDOL_PRESETS), and §3 and §7.2 of idol-9.md are untouched.
